title: Disuse is the main cause of rudimentary organs

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Disuse is the main cause of rudimentary organs

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Disuse over successive generations has been the main agency reducing organs to rudiments (as with eyes of cave animals and wings of island birds), aided by natural selection where an organ becomes injurious; because reduction occurs at maturity and is inherited at a corresponding age, rudiments remain relatively larger in the embryo.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I believe that disuse has been the main agency; that it has led in successive generations to the gradual reduction of various organs, until they have become rudimentary

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “RUDIMENTARY ORGANS; their origin explained”. Scope: organs reduced under changed habits or conditions, e.g. cave animals and island birds

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-25: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern comparative genomics can discriminate mechanisms in selected repeated losses. The Lamarckian component and global predominance claim are poorly operationalized and inadequately sampled.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across replicated losses such as cave eyes and island-bird wings, compare genomic and phenotypic signatures predicted by relaxed selection, direct selection for reduction and inherited effects of use. Estimate which process explains most reductions and whether developmental timing predicts embryonic retention.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Darwin's inherited disuse differs from modern relaxed selection and is hard to map unambiguously.

Selection, drift and developmental pleiotropy produce overlapping signatures.

The claim that disuse is the main agency requires representative global cases.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.58
data adequacy: 0.42
data existence: 0.68
discriminating power: 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Repeated evolutionary loss of unused organs is testable with phylogenies and partial trait tables, and that association is the observable part of the claim. The further claim that disuse itself is the inherited cause is not distinguished by those data from selection or drift under relaxed function. Existing resources therefore resolve a proxy pattern for well-studied cases and leave the stated agency open.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across independent origins of cave life and island flightlessness, test whether organs that are unused in the derived habitat are reduced relative to their closest surface or flying relatives, and whether the reduction is greater in adults than in embryos. The association can be confirmed or refuted; inheritance of the effects of disuse is not separated by that comparison from relaxed selection or selection against a costly organ.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Studies of eye loss and flightlessness are concentrated on a few clades, so the sample of origins is narrower than the scope.

The embryonic-size consequence needs developmental series that these phylogenies and trait tables do not contain.

Relaxed selection and positive selection for reduction predict the same association between disuse and smaller organs.
